sites.howToIntro: From the site's backend (never from the browser — that's what keeps the key out of sight):

guide.title: How to connect a site
guide.intro: Four steps. Your site's form posts to your own server, and your server forwards it here with the site's key.

create.title: Create the site here and copy the key
create.body: Use the form above. The key is shown once: save it the moment you see it. If you lose it, issue another key and revoke the old one once the site is sending with the new one.

env.title: Store the key in the site's environment
env.body: As CRMSWE_API_KEY in the .env file or in the hosting environment variables. Never in the HTML, in browser JavaScript, or in the repository.

handler.title: Paste the handler on your server
handler.body: Pick your stack below and copy the code. The form points at your own endpoint, and that endpoint is what calls CRM Swe.

verify.title: Test it with a real submission
verify.body: Fill in the form with your own number. Within seconds the contact appears and, if you set a target stage, so does the deal in the pipeline. If it doesn't, check your server log: the response says why.

security.serverSide: The key lives on the site's server. Put it in the browser and anyone can read it and write into your pipeline.
security.idempotency: Always send idempotency_key. With the same key, a retry or a double click doesn't create a duplicate contact.
security.phone: The phone number is required and is the contact's identity. We accept the Paraguayan local format (0981 123 456) and normalise it to +595.
security.spam: Add the honeypot and, if you can, Cloudflare Turnstile. Spam is stopped at your site, not inside the CRM.
security.nonBlocking: If CRM Swe doesn't answer, still show the visitor the thank-you page and record the error in your log. Never lose a lead to a timeout.

turnstile.title: Anti-bot protection (Cloudflare Turnstile)
turnstile.intro: Optional. If your site shows the Turnstile widget, paste the two keys Cloudflare gives you here. Without this the site keeps working exactly as it does today.

hookGuide.title: Connect a customer's site (without touching their server)
hookGuide.intro: For Elementor, Wix, Webflow, Zapier or Make. The customer doesn't have to install anything or give you access to their hosting: you issue the webhook URL on the site above, they paste it into their form, and that's it.
hookGuide.captureBody: As soon as the URL is in place, ask for a test submission from the customer's form. We store that submission exactly as it arrived, and then you pick from a list which field is the phone number, which is the name and which is the message. Until you do, submissions are stored as tests and don't enter the pipeline.
hookGuide.urlNote: The webhook URL is secret: anyone holding it can push leads into that site. Send it over a private channel, and revoke it from here if it leaks.

platforms.label: Elementor
steps: Open the page with the form and start editing it in Elementor.
Select the form widget and go to «Actions After Submit».
Add the «Webhook» action.
Paste the webhook URL into the «Webhook URL» field and save the page.
Send a test submission from the published page, not from the editor.

platforms.label: Wix
steps: In the Wix dashboard go to «Automations» and create a new automation.
Choose «Form is submitted» as the trigger and select the site's form.
Choose «Send an HTTP request» (or «Webhook») as the action.
Method POST, paste the webhook URL and leave the body with the form's data.
Turn the automation on and send a test submission from the published site.

platforms.label: Zapier / Make
steps: Create a Zap (or a Make scenario) with the customer's form as the trigger.
Add the «Webhooks by Zapier» → «POST» step (in Make: HTTP module → «Make a request»).
Paste the webhook URL and choose JSON as the body format.
Map the form fields into the body as they come; no renaming needed, you pick which is which here afterwards.
Turn the Zap on and run a test.

platforms.label: Other / manual
steps: Any tool that can send a POST will do: Webflow Logic, Formidable, Contact Form 7 with a webhook plugin, or the site's own backend.
POST to the webhook URL with the form contents as JSON (we also accept form-data submissions).
No special header or separate key is needed: the URL is the credential.
Send a test submission and come back here to pick the fields.

meta.title: CRM with quotes and invoicing for Swedish small businesses | CRM Swe
meta.description: Capture leads, send quotes and invoices without losing a single enquiry. Built for Swedish small businesses — email-first, GDPR from the ground up.

hero.title: Leads in. Quote out. Invoice paid.
hero.lead: A CRM that captures enquiries, sends quotes and invoices — and keeps track of what's still waiting for a reply.
hero.body: Most small businesses don't lose customers because demand is low. They lose them between systems: an enquiry sitting in an inbox, a quote nobody follows up on, an invoice that gets forgotten.
points: Every enquiry in one place, wherever it came from
Quotes and invoices with VAT calculated correctly, every time
Reminders that make sure nothing falls through the cracks
hero.asideBody: Book a short walkthrough and we'll show you how CRM Swe works for your business specifically — lead capture, quotes, invoicing and what's already built in.

problem.title: It isn't more customers you need. It's a process.
problem.body: Most businesses we talk to have neither a product problem nor a marketing problem. They have enquiries coming in from several directions, quotes that never get a reply, and invoices sent too late.
problem.bodyTwo: More marketing doesn't fix that. Organising what's already coming in does — with lead capture built on top of a foundation that holds.
problem.symptomsTitle: It shows up in concrete ways
symptoms: Enquiries by email, phone and form, with no shared list
Sent quotes nobody follows up on
Invoices written after the fact, sometimes miscalculated
No one knows how many enquiries became deals last month

meta.title: How it works | CRM Swe
meta.description: From first enquiry to a paid invoice — see how CRM Swe fits together, step by step.

header.title: Four steps, in this order
header.lead: We don't start with the feature list. We start with what actually happens to an enquiry, from the moment it arrives until the invoice is paid.
header.body: Every step stays in the system — you can always see where a deal or an invoice stands, and who did what.

items.title: 1. Lead in
items.lead: Every enquiry lands in the same place, wherever it came from.
items.body: A form on your website, the chat widget, or a manual entry — it all lands in the same pipeline with the contact details already filled in.
points: Automatic routing to the right pipeline
Nothing sitting in an inbox, forgotten

items.title: 2. Follow-up
items.lead: A deal always has an owner and a next step.
items.body: The pipeline shows where every deal stands. Reminders make sure a quote waiting for a reply doesn't go quiet on its own.
points: Full history on the contact record

items.title: 3. Quote out
items.lead: The quote is ready in minutes, with VAT calculated correctly per line.
items.body: Prices are entered excluding VAT, the customer sees net, VAT and gross clearly broken down, and a link lets the quote be approved directly.
points: VAT rate per line, never just on the total
The quote goes out as an email with a link
Approved directly by the customer, nothing to print

items.title: 4. Invoice paid
items.lead: An approved quote becomes an invoice in one click.
items.body: The invoice gets an OCR number and bankgiro details automatically, is emailed to the customer, and a payment reminder goes out if it isn't paid on time.
points: OCR and bankgiro on every invoice
A reminder if the invoice isn't paid on time

meta.title: About us | CRM Swe
meta.description: Why CRM Swe exists, and what we think a CRM for Swedish small businesses should do.

header.title: Built for how Swedish small businesses actually work
header.lead: Not a generic CRM translated into Swedish — a system where VAT, invoicing and GDPR are the foundation, not an add-on.

story.title: Most CRMs are built for sales teams, not for invoicing
story.body: Most CRM tools handle pipeline and contacts well — and stop there. Quoting and invoicing happen in a different system, often with a bookkeeper finding out about it afterwards.
story.bodyTwo: CRM Swe is built the other way round: lead capture, quotes and invoicing in the same system, with VAT calculated correctly from the start and GDPR built in, not bolted on.
story.bodyThree: The result is that nothing needs entering twice, and you always see the whole way from first contact to a paid invoice.

principles.title: Three things we don't compromise on
principles.lead: This is what decides what we build, in this order.

items.title: The VAT has to be right
items.body: The correct rate per line, never a guess on the total — that's the foundation of a legal invoice, not a detail.

items.title: Your data is yours
items.body: Export and erasure should be simple, not something you have to ask for.

items.title: Email-first
items.body: The customer should be able to get their quote and invoice without installing anything.
